questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a Spirogyra cell to show its features. *(5 marks)*
Give the functions of any four parts labelled. *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any four of:

| Part | Function |
|---|---|
| **Cell wall** | gives the cell a fixed shape, supports and protects it; fully permeable |
| **Cell membrane** | selectively permeable: controls the entry and exit of substances |
| **Cytoplasm** | site of metabolic reactions; holds the organelles |
| **Chloroplast** (with chlorophyll) | site of photosynthesis: traps light energy to make food |
| **Pyrenoid** | stores starch made by photosynthesis |
| **Nucleus** | controls all the activities of the cell; carries the hereditary material (chromosomes) |
| **Vacuole** | stores cell sap (water, salts, sugars); maintains turgor |

questions.enonce_markdown: How is Spirogyra different from an Amoeba? *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| *Spirogyra* | *Amoeba* |
|---|---|
| An alga (plant-like), made of long **filaments of many cells** | A protozoan (animal-like), a **single-celled** organism |
| Has a **cellulose cell wall** | **No cell wall**, only a cell membrane |
| Has **chloroplasts** with chlorophyll | **No chloroplasts** |
| **Autotrophic**: makes its own food by photosynthesis | **Heterotrophic (holozoic)**: engulfs food by phagocytosis |
| Stores food as **starch** | Stores food as **glycogen** |
| **Non-motile** (floats) | **Moves** by pseudopodia; irregular, changing shape |
| Has a large permanent central vacuole | Has food vacuoles and a **contractile vacuole** |

(Any six differences, each with both sides stated.)

questions.enonce_markdown: What will happen if a marine amoeba is put in a fresh water environment? *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- Fresh water has a **higher water potential** (it is **hypotonic**) than the cytoplasm of a marine amoeba, which is adapted to salty sea water.
- Water therefore enters the amoeba by **osmosis** through the partially permeable cell membrane, from the dilute surroundings to the more concentrated cytoplasm.
- The amoeba **swells** because it has **no cell wall** to resist the pressure.
- A freshwater amoeba survives because its **contractile vacuole** collects and expels the excess water; a marine amoeba is not adapted to remove water at this rate, so water enters faster than it can be expelled.
- The cell membrane is stretched until the amoeba **bursts (lyses)** and dies.
